creator_or_organization: Emerj Artificial Intelligence Research, founded by Daniel Faggella. Faggella holds a Master's in Positive Psychology from the University of Pennsylvania and is a globally recognized speaker on AI use-cases and ROI in business. He has been invited to speak at the World Bank, the United Nations, and INTERPOL, and serves as an AI Futures Group Member at OECD.ai. Emerj was originally founded as TechEmergence in 2012-2013 and rebranded to Emerj around 2019. Matthew DeMello, Senior Editor at Emerj, also serves as host and guest host on the show.
content_focus: Interviews with AI executives from Fortune 2000 companies and unicorn startups on practical AI adoption in the enterprise. Core topics include: AI strategy and ROI for business leaders, enterprise AI use-cases across industries (financial services, healthcare, supply chain, customer experience, cybersecurity), data governance and data quality for AI, agentic AI and workflow automation, post-merger data integration, AI infrastructure in compliance-heavy industries, building AI teams and organizational AI fluency, and navigating the transition from AI proof-of-concept to production deployment. Recent 2025-2026 episodes have featured executives from UBS, Alibaba.com, Prudential Insurance, SAP, UJET, Cisco (Outshift), Salesforce (Heroku), and Deloitte. The podcast takes a distinctly practitioner-focused angle: rather than discussing AI research breakthroughs, it examines how real enterprises are implementing AI, what challenges they face, and what ROI they are achieving. Emerj also produces a sister podcast, 'AI in Financial Services,' focused specifically on banking and insurance AI use-cases.
target_audience: Non-technical business leaders, C-suite executives, enterprise AI decision-makers, consultants, and entrepreneurs seeking to understand practical AI adoption. Explicitly designed for people who need to find AI opportunities, align AI capabilities with business strategy, and deliver ROI without requiring a technical background.
format_and_length: Audio podcast, approximately 25-30 minutes per episode (average ~28 minutes). Interview format with one guest per episode. Available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, iHeart, Podbean, and all major podcast platforms. Over 870 episodes in the archive spanning more than a decade.
accessibility_for_non_engineers: High. The podcast is explicitly built for non-technical business leaders. Daniel Faggella frames every conversation around business outcomes, ROI, and strategic decisions rather than technical architectures or algorithms. Guests are typically C-suite executives or senior directors who discuss AI in terms of organizational impact, competitive advantage, and operational efficiency. Technical jargon is consistently translated into business language. Episode titles reflect this approach: 'Data Quality Assessment for Non-Technical Leaders,' 'Lifting the AI Fluency of Enterprise Teams at Scale,' 'Why Post-Merger Integrations Fail Without Data Governance.' Business students with no engineering background would find this highly accessible and directly relevant to their entrepreneurial thinking.
signal_to_noise_ratio: High. The podcast benefits from Emerj's position as an AI market research firm, meaning episodes are grounded in research-backed questions rather than surface-level hype. Faggella has conducted nearly a thousand interviews with Fortune 500 AI leaders, giving him deep contextual knowledge that produces sharper, more specific questions. Each episode is focused on a single topic or use-case, avoiding the 'AI news roundup' format that dilutes insight. The 28-minute average length ensures conversations stay focused. The main limitation is that as a market research firm, Emerj has business relationships with some enterprise AI vendors, which could introduce subtle promotional bias in guest selection.
unique_value_proposition: The longest-running AI business podcast, with over 870 episodes and more than a decade of continuous coverage since before the current AI boom. While most AI podcasts focus on Silicon Valley startups and frontier research, Emerj uniquely targets the enterprise AI adoption perspective — how Fortune 2000 companies actually implement, manage, and derive ROI from AI. The podcast is backed by Emerj's position as an AI market research firm, which provides a systematic, research-informed approach to guest selection and questioning that distinguishes it from personality-driven shows. No other AI podcast offers this depth of coverage specifically focused on enterprise AI decision-making for non-technical leaders.
free_or_paid: Freemium. The main AI in Business Podcast episodes are available for free on all major podcast platforms. Emerj Plus membership ($7 for 30-day trial, then $59/month or $408/year) provides access to the full library of interviews, articles, use-case breakdowns, downloadable resources, and the AI Consulting Podcast. Most listeners can access the core podcast content without paying.
source_reliability: High. Emerj is a dedicated AI market research firm, not a media company or individual blogger, which provides an institutional foundation for editorial quality. Guests are verified senior executives at named Fortune 2000 companies and well-known startups, providing primary-source enterprise perspectives. Daniel Faggella's credentials include speaking engagements at the World Bank, United Nations, and INTERPOL, and he is recognized by the OECD as an AI expert. His research has been cited by TechCrunch, Inc, Forbes, and Xconomy. The main bias to note is that Emerj's business model involves selling AI market research to enterprises, which could influence the optimistic framing of enterprise AI adoption and the selection of guests from companies that may be Emerj clients or prospects.
relevance_for_entrepreneurs: High. This podcast provides entrepreneurs with direct insight into how large enterprises think about, evaluate, and implement AI — knowledge that is essential for anyone building AI products or services targeting enterprise customers. Specific value includes: (1) understanding enterprise procurement decision-making, compliance requirements, and integration challenges that AI startups must navigate to win B2B deals; (2) learning which AI use-cases are delivering measurable ROI across industries, helping entrepreneurs identify validated market opportunities; (3) hearing from enterprise AI buyers about their pain points, vendor evaluation criteria, and build-vs-buy decisions; (4) gaining a realistic picture of enterprise AI maturity across sectors, avoiding the hype cycle and focusing on where genuine demand exists. For students at Sorbonne's M2 Entrepreneuriat, this podcast bridges the gap between AI technology and enterprise business reality.
actionable_insight_level: Medium-High. Each episode typically focuses on a specific enterprise AI use-case or challenge, providing concrete examples of what works and what does not in real deployments. Guests share specific frameworks, organizational strategies, and lessons learned from implementing AI at scale. However, the insights are framed for Fortune 2000 executives and may require translation for early-stage entrepreneurs or smaller companies. The podcast excels at providing 'here is how big companies actually buy and deploy AI' insights, which are highly actionable for B2B AI entrepreneurs.
session_mapping: S3 (Projects) and S4 (Business Models/Strategy). S3: strong alignment with CRISP-DM process understanding, build-vs-buy decisions, data quality assessment, and managing AI projects in enterprise contexts. S4: provides real-world examples of AI business models, enterprise AI strategy, unit economics of AI deployment, and scaling AI solutions. Also relevant to S1 (Fundamentals) for understanding the enterprise AI landscape and to S5 (Ethics/Governance) through episodes on data governance, compliance, and responsible AI in regulated industries.
ecosystem_position: Analytical and primary source. Emerj occupies a unique niche as an AI market research firm with a media arm, sitting between pure journalism and consulting. The podcast functions as a primary source of enterprise AI executive perspectives — guests share firsthand experience with AI deployment that is not available through news coverage or research papers. Emerj's research methodology adds an analytical layer, as episodes are informed by their broader market research across hundreds of Fortune 500 companies. The podcast complements startup-focused shows like No Priors or All-In by providing the enterprise buyer's perspective rather than the investor or founder perspective. It also serves as a pipeline for Emerj's paid research products, positioning the free podcast as a top-of-funnel content channel for their market research business.
